newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese firm develops paving blocks that eat smog.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firm develops paving blocks that eat smog.

text.p: A Japanese firm has developed concrete paving blocks that it says can clean the air of nitrogen oxides, a major pollutant from traffic exhausts.

Mitsubishi Materials Corp, one of Japan's leading manufacturers of metals and cement, said on Monday that experiments showed its specially treated concrete blocks removed 80 percent of nitrogen oxides from the air when tested in containers in a laboratory.
The blocks' surface contains titanium oxide, a substance that when hit by sunlight undergoes a catalytic reaction that removes nitrogen oxides from the surrounding air, it said.

It added that the pollutant-absorbing properties of the concrete would be long-lasting, as the small quantities of nitric acid that build up on the surface when nitrogen oxides are absorbed would be washed away by rainwater.
The company said 50 square metres of the paving blocks had been installed on sidewalks along a highway in Osaka Prefecture in western Japan as an experiment to evaluate the material.
A unit of the company will begin to manufacture and sell the concrete blocks in January through a network of franchises that includes 18 firms.
The blocks will sell for 12,000 yen ($105) per cubic metre, about the same price as more expensive conventional paving blocks, the company said.
It is also studying other potential uses of the technology, such as concrete sound barriers used along major highways. ($1=114 yen)
